subject.title: [Feature]: Configurable batching/aggregation of outbound Telegram notifications

question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in outbound Telegram notification digest policy, and should that policy live in the Telegram plugin, shared outbound delivery, or a plugin/hook extension surface?
rationale: The missing behavior is source-backed, but the correct contract affects config shape, delivery timing, urgent error bypass, media/thread semantics, persistence, and core-versus-plugin ownership.

options.title: Define durable digest policy
options.body: Choose the owner seam, config names, bypass rules, and SQLite-backed flush semantics before implementation.

options.title: Expose extension hook only
options.body: Keep core lean by adding or documenting only the hook/API surface needed for an external digest plugin.

options.title: Keep immediate delivery
options.body: Treat throttling, streaming coalescing, and existing inbound queue controls as the supported anti-spam mechanisms and later close or narrow this request.

recommendation.title: Define durable digest policy
recommendation.body: Choose the owner seam, config names, bypass rules, and SQLite-backed flush semantics before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans shared delivery lifecycle, Telegram throttling, config policy, and product boundary, where steipete has the strongest history signal.
